newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Oct 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Oct 30.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- Savings rates in the private sector continues to decline. Total savings rate has hovered below total investment rate for the past six years, contributing to increased foreign borrowing and widening current-account deficit, according to Bank of Korea.
- North Korea is building a 1,000-ton submarine, and the submarine infiltration last month was part of Pyongyang's war preparation, said a captured North Korean commando.

- Opposition lawmaker questioning the administration of Economic Affairs during parliamentary question-answer session calls for interest rate cut and a shakeup of economic ministers, replacing them with suprapartisan figures.
- Prosecutors, investigating corruption charges against Former Defense Minister Lee Yang-ho, have uncovered 300 million won worth of bonds concealed by the former defense chief.
- President Kim Young-sam is expected to meet with U.S. president Bill Clinton during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting scheduled to open in the Philippines November 22.
- The U.S. dollar continues to gain record strength against the Korean won, with the exchange rate reaching 834.5 won per dollar on Tuesday.
- The Korean economy seems to be off the track for a soft landing hoped for by the government as exports are rapidly losing steam, according to an economic forecast released yesterday.
- The sole captured crew member of a North Korean spy submarine that ran aground on a South Korean beach last month said that North Korea is building 1,000-ton submarines for infiltration.
- North Korea is constructing a 1,000-ton submarine which will be used to operate behind enemy lines and land commandos to disrupt order in rear areas.
- The Korean economy is forecast to grow by 6.5 percent next year, down from this year's estimated 6.8 percent, according to the state-funded Korea Development Institute.
